A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DaWin and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A.1–A.5. The material supports a reliable comparison; v4’s unresolved citations are identifiable document changes.

before.justification: v3 reports original DaWin evaluations on ImageNet distribution shifts and eight multi-task benchmarks, alongside pilot experiments, runtime measurements, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v4 retains the original DaWin benchmark results, pilot experiments, runtime measurements, and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: The entropy-based coefficients, domain offsets, mixture modeling, and multi-task formulation are unchanged. Sections 3 and A.1 retain the same procedure and Algorithm 1.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ImageNet and its five distribution-shift benchmarks, plus the same eight multi-task datasets. No training or evaluation domain or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the main and appendix experiments, including WiSE-FT, Model Soups, Model Stock, AdaMerging/++, Pareto Merging, and the alternative coefficient methods.

E3.justification: Both versions retain the same CLIP backbones, top-1 accuracy evaluation, validation-based temperature scaling, and interpolation searches. Mixture-component settings remain 3/5/2 for the three robust fine-tuning backbones and 1 for multi-task evaluation.

E4.justification: The expertise-metric and offset ablations, sample-size sensitivity, calibration ablation, coefficient analyses, and expert/nonexpert model-pool tests are retained unchanged, including Figure 5 and Appendix Tables A–G.

E5.justification: Seed-related implementation information and statistical reporting are unchanged. Neither version adds or revises repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Numerical results and plotted findings match throughout. For example, DaWin retains 78.70% ID and 54.36% OOD accuracy in Table 2 and 86.3% average accuracy in Table 6; appendix result entries also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The definitions, coefficient equations, mixture-model derivations, entropy-valley hypothesis, Lemma 6.1, and Appendix A.4 proof are unchanged. Removing a supporting citation in A.3 does not revise the mathematical argument.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free dynamic interpolation, entropy-based expertise estimation, mixture-model efficiency, and performance across 14 classification tasks.

C2.justification: The explanations of entropy-based weighting and empirical behavior are unchanged. Appendix A.5 retains the restricted vision-model validation scope, inference-cost limitation, and future directions; its citation losses do not alter those interpretations.

D1.justification: Algorithm details, checkpoint sources, hyperparameters, calibration instructions, and hardware/runtime information remain unchanged in the appendices. The abstract’s code-access link also has the same destination.

R1.justification: Seven bibliography entries disappear: Model Ratatouille and works by Snell, Jaech, Muennighoff, OpenAI, Zhang, and Oh supporting Appendix A.5. Their corresponding citations become unresolved question marks in A.3 and A.5. The main related-work positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 makes limited grammatical and wording edits, such as adding 'be' to 'can be effectively estimated' and correcting 'wall-block' to 'wall-clock.' Section organization and the overall narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure F’s caption corrects a stray character in 'distribution shifts,' and the shortened bibliography changes reference-page spacing and placement. Figures, table structures, axes, and legends otherwise remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The modest copyediting gains are outweighed by lost attribution: v3 supplies identifiable citations for linear mode connectivity in A.3 and test-time scaling and multimodal OOD limitations in A.5, whereas v4 displays '?' or '???' and omits seven corresponding references. This makes those retained claims harder to trace. The scientific methods and empirical evidence remain unchanged, so the overall decline is limited.
